newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's ENI hits road for third chunk sale.
newsitem.headline: Italy's ENI hits road for third chunk sale.

text.p: Italian energy giant ENI on Monday began a round of roadshows ahead of a sale later this month of a further chunk of some one billion shares in Europe's third largest oil and gas company.
"All indications are for another great success," ENI Chairman Guglielmo Moscato told a news conference after the first of a series of presentations to institutional investors.

The Italian Treasury, which currently holds 69 percent of ENI, the largest publicly traded company in the country, on Saturday announced it aimed to sell at least 12.5 percent of the group in the biggest international share offer so far this year.
The ENI3 offer will rise to 14.4 percent if demand warrants it, and if all the stock is sold the Treasury will raise some 10 trillion lire ($5.9 billion) at current market prices.
"This operation is sure to be welcomed as well as the last sale," said one Milan equity trader.

The first ENI global offering took place in December 1995 when ENI's shareholder the Treasury sold a 15 percent stake which raised $3.95 billion. A second sale of 16 percent in November 1996 brought in $5.9 billion.

ENI shares have risen by nearly 70 percent since the first sale at 5,250 lire each and last Friday's close on the Milan stock exchange at 8,739 lire. ENI American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) are also traded in New York.
ENI stock closed 1.68 percent higher on the Milan Bourse on Monday at 8,885 lire.
ENI posted record group net profit of 4.45 trillion lire in 1996 and sees further improvement for this year.
A minimum 400 million shares will be offered to the Italian public from June 23 to 27. The price will be set on June 28.
A further 300 million are earmarked for Italian and foreign institutional investors outside north America, with some 150 million shares reserved for U.S. and Canadian institutions.
Around 130 million extra shares have been set aside under a so-called "green shoe" option in case of strong demand.

ENI Managing Director Franco Bernabei told the news conference that the group, the world's seventh largest publicly traded oil and gas company, was "one of the great international success stories of recent years".
Underlining the group's efforts to streamline its structure and improve efficiency, he said this third tranche sale marked a turning point in ENI's development.

This would now be focused on growth rather than rationalisation, the aim to transform ENI from an Italian company into a global multinational, and concentrating on core activities pointed up by the recently announced incorporation of ENI's Agip exploration and production unit.
"Upstream activities are now a crucial part of group industrial strategy," Bernabei said.

The group aimed to continue with its rigorous cost-cutting policy to increase margins. Bernabei said if given the right conditions, ENI could possibly see cost savings of about one trillion lire in the period up to the year 2000. He declined to go into details.
"We have reduced costs immensely over the last five years and reorganised personnel from top to bottom. The group's clear determination has given us international credibility," he added.
ENI has operations in 84 countries and has some 83,000 employees.
Under the terms of the third tranche offer, the Treasury is committed not to offer more ENI stock to the market for six months. The "lock-up" clause with previous tranches was nine months.
Italy's IMI bank and CSFB are global coordinators for the offer. Share trading is set to start on Tuesday, July 1. $ = 1,687 lire
